name: Treaty with the Menominee, 1831 (Stambaugh Treaty)
aka: Treaty of Washington with the Menominee, February 8, 1831
promises: At the President's request, and while protesting that they owed the New York Indians nothing, the Menominee agreed that part of their land west of the Fox River could be set apart as a home for the New York Indians who moved there within three years; for this the United States would pay the Menominee $20,000, paid $5,000 at a time (Articles First and Second).
The Menominee ceded their country southeast of Lake Winnebago, the Fox River and Green Bay (Article Third).

A tract on the west side of the Fox River would be set apart as the Menominee's future home, with five farmers and five women teachers for ten years, $10,000 for the Menominee's houses and $3,000 for the farmers' houses, household articles and livestock once they settled, $8,000 in clothing and $1,000 in provisions within six months, and $6,000 a year for twelve years (Article Fourth).
The school fund of the 1827 treaty was raised by $500 a year and continued for ten years (Article Fifth).

The Menominee could hunt and fish on the ceded land east of the Fox River and Green Bay as before until it was surveyed and offered for sale, and their remaining land west of the Fox River would stay their hunting ground until the President chose to extinguish their title, at an annuity he would fix (Article Sixth).
landTaken: Royce areas 158 to 162 in Wisconsin, including the cession southeast of Lake Winnebago and the tract for the New York Indians, whose boundaries Royce shows as modified by the treaty of October 27, 1832. No acreage for the cession was found in a source opened.
compensation: $20,000 for the New York Indians' tract, and the houses, goods, services and $6,000 annuity of Article Fourth.
today: Royce records that the Senate ratified this treaty only with provisos that set aside two townships on the east side of Lake Winnebago for the Stockbridge and Munsee and one for the Brothertown, and ran a new line for the New York Indians' tract. The Menominee's later reservation came from later treaties, not this one.

sources.title: Treaty with the Menominee, 1831 (Kappler vol. 2, p. 319), 7 Stat. 342
sources.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Tribal Treaties Database

sources.title: Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (1899), schedule pp. 728-731, areas 158-162

openQuestions: No breach was found, but the search was limited: the OSU Indian Claims Commission collection returned no decisions for menominee, menomonee, menomini or menominees, so the Menominee's land claims (which may have gone to the Court of Claims under a special act) were not reached.

Leads for a deeper pass: whether the farmers, teachers, houses and $6,000 annuity of Article Fourth were provided; whether the Senate provisos were accepted by the Menominee in the treaty of October 27, 1832; and Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin v. Thompson (7th Cir. 1998) on the Article Sixth hunting and fishing privilege (161 F.3d 449), which could not be opened on 2026-11-08; its holding should be read before the file is deepened.
The Menominee Indian Tribe's website has pages for the treaties of 1836, 1848, 1854 and 1856 but none for 1831 found on 2026-11-08; no nation account was found.
